verdicts.evidence: 10-seed runs on the paper's Linear DGP (K=3, n_k=2000, alpha=0.1) show MDCP worst-case coverage of 0.905 (classification) and 0.909 (regression), both above the 0.90 nominal level; the max-p baseline over-covers (0.944/0.939) as expected.

500 seeded finite-measure LP instances (3 sources, 24 outcomes, alpha=0.1) solved via scipy.optimize.linprog show max primal-dual gap 2.23e-8, max complementary-slackness error 2.23e-8, max superlevel-structure violation 1.26e-8, with active sources in 500/500 instances.

8 sample sizes (100–25,000) × 20 seeds on 64-outcome categorical distributions show shared-score error dropping from 3.92 to 0.392 (Spearman −1.000) and calibrated-set symmetric difference from 18.45 to 1.80 (within oracle boundary of 3); frozen-weight destructive control fails to converge, isolating the theorem's consistency assumption.

Measured classification set reduction is 4.73% (SE 1.68) vs claimed 34.39%; even a cheating oracle constant-lambda yields only 13.49%. Significant optimizer deviations (full-batch Adam, no scipy/sklearn, parametric fits) are a live confound not ruled out.

Measured regression set reduction is 8.71% (SE 1.85) vs claimed 22.44%; oracle constant-lambda yields 11.91%. Same optimizer deviations as Claim 4 prevent attributing the shortfall to the method itself.
No FMoW images, DenseNet-121 checkpoint, or six-region prediction artifacts were used; the logbook explicitly states the claim was not attempted.

overall: The logbook provides concrete numerical support for the three theoretical claims (Theorems 1–3) via direct experiments on the paper's synthetic DGP and finite-alphabet instantiations with rigorous KKT and convergence checks. The two empirical efficiency claims show measured reductions far below the paper's reported values, but legitimate optimizer deviations prevent a definitive refutation, and the FMoW claim is entirely unaddressed.
